title: Now, Not Next
author: Josh Brake
summary: Josh Brake opens with a Disneyland observation -- a parent on the It's a Small World ride scrolling Lightning Lane openings at other attractions -- to name 'destination sickness': the modern pathology of always planning the next thing at the expense of the present. He extends this to college campuses where students enter already worried about life after graduation. Drawing on a podcast conversation with Dave Evans (co-author of 'How to Live a Meaningful Life'), Brake recounts an ICU nurse's story about accomplished patients in their mid-50s dying in despair after realizing they 'ran through' their lives chasing the next thing and missed the whole thing. Evans offers three antidotes: (1) Reframe from 'got to' to 'get to' -- daily obligations look different in the right frame; (2) Do your best without attaching to results -- effort is in your control, outcomes often aren't; (3) 'Be here now' -- there is nowhere else to be but here. Brake applies this to his own sabbatical coming to a close, trying to approach upcoming opportunities with gratitude rather than obligation. The essay is a genuine attempt at personal accountability about a problem easier to spot in others.
points: * Destination sickness: the pathology of always obsessing over the next thing -- next ride, next semester, next job, next salary -- at the expense of present experience; it disguises itself as prudence but is rooted in discontentment. * The ICU nurse's warning: the accomplished patients dying in their 50s had been running through their lives chasing the next thing and at the end looked back to find they had missed the whole thing. * Antidote 1 -- reframe from 'got to' to 'get to': the same obligation looks entirely different when understood as a privilege rather than a requirement. * Antidote 2 -- do your best without attachment to results: effort is within your control, outcomes often are not; studying does not guarantee acing the test, consistent writing does not guarantee every essay will be great. * Antidote 3 -- 'Be here now': there is no way to skip ahead, and how much better to be present in each moment and look for what it has to offer, rather than already living in the next one.
quotes: Everyone is already thinking about the next thing.
And they look back at all the things they ran through and they realized they missed the whole thing.
If this doesn't stop you in your tracks today, it should.
The antidote to destination sickness is not complicated, but that doesn't mean it's easy.
